# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 17 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 34 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_017_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 17

**1** Jesus said: "I will give you what no eye has seen and what no ear has heard and what no hand has touched and what has never arisen in the human heart."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**Four-member list** — consensus. Thomas's unique fourth member (the hand) expands the Pauline tradition with a tactile dimension. The completeness is: sight / hearing / touch / thought — all human sensory and cognitive channels exhausted.

**"Arisen in the human heart"** — LOGOS preferred over PNEUMA's "entered any human mind" and EMET's "occurred to the human mind." The Coptic uses the heart-metaphor (*hēt nrōme*); "arisen in the human heart" preserves both the cardiac idiom and the dynamic of something arising.

**Synoptic Parallels:**
- 1 Cor 2:9: "What no eye has seen, nor ear heard, nor the human heart conceived" — Paul cites this as scripture ("as it is written"), but the Isaiah source (64:4; 65:17) does not match. This may be a Jesus-tradition Paul knows; Thomas preserves a more complete version.
- Isaiah 64:4 (LXX): partial parallel
- No direct Synoptic parallel (Matthew/Mark/Luke do not preserve this saying)

**Theological Note:** The saying is eschatological and mystical simultaneously. Thomas places it in the collection not as a future promise about heaven but as the description of what the sayings themselves provide to those who interpret them (cf. Saying 1).
